Permutation test within blocks

Source: R/blkprm.R
blkprm.Rd

The randomisation test of a treatment effect in a blocked (or stratified, or matched) experiment: the treatment labels are permuted within each block, so that every arrangement keeps each block's number of treated units, as the design randomised them, and the observed statistic is compared with its values over the arrangements (Rosenbaum 2002, ch. 2; Good 2005, sec. 3.6).

Usage

blkprm(
  data,
  y,
  d,
  block,
  stat = c("diff", "strat"),
  alt = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  nperm = 2000,
  exact = FALSE,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'blkprm'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit.

y

The name of the outcome column (numbers).

d

The name of the treatment column: 0 or 1 (or FALSE, TRUE), both present.

block

The name of the block column (labels).

stat

"diff" (the difference in means) or "strat" (the block-weighted mean of the blocks' differences).

alt

The alternative: "two.sided", "greater" (the treated higher) or "less".

nperm

The number of arrangements drawn: a whole number from 1 to 10000000 (not used with exact).

exact

TRUE to enumerate every arrangement.

seed

NULL (drawn from R's generator, so set.seed() fixes it) or a whole number from 0 to 2147483647; not used with exact.

x

An object of class blkprm.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class blkprm, a list: est (the observed statistic), p, nperm (the arrangements used), nge (those at least as extreme), nblock, stat, alt, exact, dist (the permuted values) and seed (NA with exact).

Details

stat = "diff" is the difference between the mean outcome of the treated and of the controls over all units; stat = "strat" is the mean over blocks of the blocks' own differences, weighted by the blocks' sizes, the stratified estimate of the average effect (every block then needs treated and control units). With exact = TRUE every arrangement is enumerated (at most 1000000) and p is the share at least as extreme as the observed value; otherwise nperm arrangements are drawn from the package's generator and p = (1 + k) / (1 + nperm), k of them at least as extreme, which is never 0 (Phipson and Smyth 2010). Values within 1e-9 (|T| + max|y|) of the observed T count as at least as extreme, so that arrangements equal to it in exact arithmetic are never lost to rounding.

References

Rosenbaum, P. R. (2002). Observational Studies, 2nd ed. Springer. doi:10.1007/978-1-4757-3692-2

Good, P. I. (2005). Permutation, Parametric, and Bootstrap Tests of Hypotheses, 3rd ed. Springer. doi:10.1007/b138696

Phipson, B. and Smyth, G. K. (2010). Permutation p-values should never be zero: calculating exact p-values when permutations are randomly drawn. Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology, 9(1), 39. doi:10.2202/1544-6115.1585

Examples

set.seed(4)
d <- data.frame(site = rep(1:6, each = 4), t = rep(c(1, 0, 1, 0), 6))
d$y <- d$site + 0.8 * d$t + rnorm(24, sd = 0.5)
blkprm(d, "y", "t", "site", nperm = 999, seed = 1)
#> blkprm: difference in means 0.9952, p = 0.001 (two.sided, 999 arrangements within 6 blocks)
blkprm(d[1:12, ], "y", "t", "site", stat = "strat", exact = TRUE)$p
#> [1] 0.01851852
